assessment.nobel_worthiness: Turns a biological process, ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis, into a designable chemical reaction: bifunctional degraders and molecular glues hijack E3 ligases to remove a chosen protein. Conceptually original and a general tool for biologists, with direct relevance to cancer and genetic disease.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated heterobifunctional degraders; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains the glue-degrader mechanism. Ciulli (VHL ligands), Sakamoto, Gray and others are also major, so a three-person cut is a real compromise.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the principle, degraders are in advanced clinical trials, and the mechanism is understood at the ternary-complex structural level. Timing looks right, though clinical proof of benefit is still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on PROTACs, on the thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue mechanism, or both.
Credit among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray is contested; I am relying on memory of the literature, not verification.
Clinical efficacy of degraders is not yet fully established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another on genomic DNA without double-strand breaks, using engineered deaminases. This is nucleobase chemistry made into a general tool, with major therapeutic implications and clearly distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory designed and led the cytidine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainee authors; Nishida and Kondo reported a related cytidine-deaminase fusion. A single-laureate configuration is defensible, but credit for the Nishida/Kondo work is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely across organisms, with first clinical uses of base editing in patients, so recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 prize may make the committee cautious.
Nishida/Kondo priority question.
Long-term safety of editing, including off-target deamination, is still being measured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A single nucleic-acid strand is read electrically as it passes through a protein pore. This converts DNA and RNA chemistry into a direct physical readout, and it enabled long-read sequencing and direct detection of modified bases, which matters for nucleotide and genome-stability research.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandon, Branton and Deamer showed that a strand can translocate through alpha-hemolysin; Bayley engineered the pores and chemistry for base discrimination; Akeson demonstrated the enzyme-controlled ratcheting that made sequencing practical. Choosing three of five is difficult, and I am unsure of the current status of every credited person.
assessment.maturity: Strongly and independently reproduced, commercially deployed, and used in routine genomics and in the field. Mature.
uncertainties: Credit among the five credited names is uncertain.
Whether some credited individuals are still living (a prize cannot be awarded posthumously) is unconfirmed by me.
Commercial development was led by industry, which may blur academic attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, made possible by reversible-terminator and sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry, transformed biology and medicine. Its core is nucleotide chemistry, and it supplies the data behind much of genome-stability and cancer research.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the Solexa sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry and platform; Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing was the first commercial massively parallel system; Ju contributed reversible-terminator chemistry and Mayer the early parallel-sequencing concepts. A fair configuration is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and ubiquitous, with decades of confirmation. If anything the prize is late, and the committee may view it as better suited to medicine or as already covered by the 1980 sequencing prize.
uncertainties: Contested allocation among Balasubramanian, Klenerman, Rothberg, Ju and Mayer.
Whether the committee judges it chemistry enough, or too close to the 1980 and 1958 sequencing awards.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat showed that a mutant cysteine in KRAS G12C can be targeted covalently, which opened a protein long considered undruggable. He also pioneered chemical-genetic analog-sensitive kinases. This is clear chemistry with biological and clinical impact, in a single, clean discovery.
assessment.attribution: A single credited name, so attribution is simple. Industrial teams then developed the approved drugs, and the committee would need to decide that Shokat's academic work is the decisive step.
assessment.maturity: Sotorasib and adagrasib are approved and the principle has been taken up by independent groups. Recognition is plausible now, but the longer-term durability of resistance is still being studied.
uncertainties: Resistance to KRAS G12C inhibitors limits clinical durability.
Role of industry teams in the realised drugs.
Only one laureate, which makes a shared prize configuration with others less likely.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made routine, automated synthesis of DNA possible and is the reaction underlying primers, probes, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide drugs. It is foundational nucleotide chemistry on which sequencing, PCR and genome engineering depend.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method and its solid-phase automation. The supplied credit also names Leroy Hood for the automated synthesizer, but the decisive chemical invention is Caruthers'; earlier phosphotriester and phosphite work by others is a possible complication.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature, with decades of independent confirmation. The risk is that recognition is long overdue, so the committee may see it as historical.
uncertainties: Prior contributions (Letsinger, Khorana, Beaucage) might compete for credit.
Whether Caruthers alone is acceptable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase pairs allow cells to incorporate non-canonical amino acids with new chemistry, effectively reprogramming translation. This is a general tool for biologists and a clean example of making a biological process a defined chemical reaction.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the first routine genetic-code expansion in living organisms; Chin extended it to multicellular systems, multiple codons and ribosome engineering. Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama are also important, so the configuration is open.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and adopted in protein engineering and chemical biology, with growing therapeutic applications. Mature in the core method, though its broader impact is still emerging.
uncertainties: Credit among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama is not cleanly separable.
Therapeutic impact remains limited so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the delivery chemistry that makes siRNA and mRNA medicines work, including the COVID-19 vaccines. Importance and impact are very large. The 2023 medicine prize recognized the mRNA modifications, not the delivery chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Madden, Hope, MacLachlan) developed ionizable-lipid formulation methods and the pH-dependent mechanism of encapsulation; Anderson and Langer contributed lipid libraries and combinatorial discovery. Distributing credit across many groups is hard.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated by approved siRNA and mRNA products, with independent confirmation. Timing is reasonable, but the surrounding mRNA recognition may make the committee hesitate.
uncertainties: Highly diffuse credit across academic and industrial authors.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as medicine.
Mechanistic detail of endosomal escape is still debated.
